title: por_comparator VPOR-up / VPOR-down / hysteresis over process x temperature (quasi-static VDD sweep)
claim: Issue #102 -- NOT a spec claim. Evidence for DR-003 rows 4/5 ([TBD-2] VPOR-up/VPOR-down, [TBD-3] hysteresis): records, for the unchanged design/por_comparator.sch, the VDD at which POR_RAW changes state on a quasi-static constant-dVDD/dt UP sweep (VPOR-up) and DOWN sweep (VPOR-down), their difference (hysteresis), and the margin of VPOR-up against the DR-001 2.97 V low rail, across {tt, ss, ff, sf, fs} x {-40, 27, 125 C}. Each primary sweep rate is paired with a half-rate quasi-staticity guard. Numbers are PROPOSALS for a follow-on DR-003 amendment; spec/ is not edited and nothing here relaxes the ratified spec.
provenance_source: sim/por-comparator-thresholds/testbench/*.sch (DUT: design/netlist/por_comparator.spice, the committed export of design/por_comparator.sch)
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim; no mismatch Monte Carlo)

passive_skew.note: SUPPLEMENT, recorded separately (run --axis passive-skew; record ids end in -passive-skew). sky130's ll/hh .lib sections are tt MOS/BJT with parameters_res_low/high + cap_low/high; per sim/pdk.json they are the ONLY sections that move sky130_fd_pr__res_xhigh_po sheet resistance (tt/ss/ff/sf/fs all include parameters_res_nom). klt passes a bare process string through as `.lib <models.lib> <process>`, so the axis is reachable. The divider (XRTOP/XRBOT/XRHYS) is all xhigh_po, so a ratio cancellation is expected to first order; this axis measures it rather than assuming it.

rails.source: DR-001 supply flavor (3.3 V +/-10 %); spec/porting-plan.md Sec2.3 margin arithmetic

sweep.construction: V(VDD) = min(peak, rate*t, max(0, 2*peak - rate*t)): UP from a physical 0 V start at +rate V/s to the 3.63 V peak (the DR-001 high rail), then DOWN at -rate V/s to 0 V. Total sweep time 2*peak/rate is derived from the rate, never a fixed duration (gf180 DR-021 confound). VDD is the swept variable, so there is no separate supply axis; the klt corners.supply_v axis carries only the single sweep-peak value. Maximum time step 20 us = 2 mV of VDD at 100 V/s (1 mV at the 50 V/s half-rate guard).

rates.status: EXPLORATORY quasi-static choice, not a specification envelope. An uncommitted pilot at 1 kV/s (primary) / 500 V/s (guard) showed the extracted edges shifting with rate by several mV (VPOR-up later, VPOR-down earlier: a response lag of order 10 us, larger with the real bias_core), enough to trip the 10 mV guard on the real-bias variant; the primary rate was therefore lowered to 100 V/s so the lag is ~10x smaller than the guard tolerance. The half-rate guard still decides, per corner, whether the result is quasi-static.
rates.construction: dVDD/dt is constant and derived from the rate; each rate gets one klt request covering all 15 process x temperature points.

polarity.note: Expected direction of POR_RAW crossing 0.5*VDD during the UP sweep and DOWN sweep respectively; a crossing in the other direction is reported as wrong_direction, not accepted.

ideal-bias.description: PRIMARY. Comparator + divider + hysteresis switch isolated from bias_core.
ideal-bias.bias_treatment: IDEAL: IBIAS = ideal 1 uA current source into the mirror-input node; VREF = ideal 1.25 V clipped to v(VDD); BIAS_OK = v(VDD) (asserted at every supply). Chosen because the primary question is the divider ratio, the comparator offset and the XRHYS/XMHSW hysteresis network; an ideal VREF/IBIAS removes the bias_core's own process/temperature/startup behavior (issue #86 open items) from the threshold numbers. 1 uA / 1.25 V are the bias_core intended-branch values (sim/bias-core-startup).

real-bias-core.description: SECOND, separately-reported variant: the real design/bias_core drives IBIAS, VREF and BIAS_OK.
real-bias-core.bias_treatment: REAL bias_core (design/netlist/bias_core.spice) on the same VDD supplies IBIAS, VREF and BIAS_OK, so the actual VREF(P,T,VDD) and delivered IBIAS move the edges. Never mixed with the ideal-bias table; shows how far the real reference dependence displaces the thresholds.

definitions.VPOR-up / VPOR-down: interpolated VDD at which POR_RAW crosses 0.5*VDD (POR_RAW high = above half the instantaneous supply) during the UP / DOWN segment; segments split at the VDD maximum; state evaluated only for VDD >= 1.0 V
definitions.hysteresis: VPOR-up - VPOR-down at the same process/temperature
definitions.no transition: a segment in which POR_RAW does not change state is reported as no_transition (with the state it stayed in), not omitted; hysteresis is then NO_RESULT
definitions.resolution: an edge is accepted only if the two samples bracketing it differ by <= 10 mV of VDD; otherwise UNRESOLVED
definitions.quasi-static guard: VPOR-up and VPOR-down at the primary rate must agree with the half-rate sweep within 10 mV (stated tolerance, chosen for this campaign, not ratified); otherwise the corner is reported RATE-DEPENDENT and excluded from the binding-corner table
definitions.binding corner: the process/temperature point that sets the minimum or maximum of each metric over the corners with a clean, rate-consistent result

absent_coverage: The passive-skew (ll/hh) axis is covered only as a separately-recorded supplement on tt MOS (ll/hh x 3 temperatures); combined MOS-corner x resistor-skew points (e.g. ss MOS with res_high) are NOT run -- sky130.lib.spice has no such combined section and no multi-section bundle was built for this campaign.
Mismatch Monte Carlo (comparator input offset, divider ratio mismatch) is NOT run; the numbers are corner values of the nominal drawn circuit, not a distribution.
Sweep rates other than 100 V/s (and its 50 V/s guard) are not simulated; supply-ramp-rate sensitivity of the assembled block is covered by sim/supply-ramp-top.
Post-layout parasitics are not included (schematic-level netlist).
The ideal-bias variant uses a constant 1 uA IBIAS and a 1.25 V VREF at every corner; real bias_core spread is only shown by the separately-reported real-bias-core variant.
ngspice_note: The fleet runner (klt 0.5.0, ngspice 46) ignores options.ngspice_init, so the equivalent of sim/spiceinit's ng_nomodcheck is set by a .control block carried in the netlist body ('set ng_nomodcheck'). Local ngspice is 42; a single-point local cross-check is recorded.
